Story Forge — The Library (spec 008, Phase 7) · addendum L1–L9 to S91–S104 · draft for sign-off

Why this page exists. docs/mockups/anvil-workbench-codex.html (S91–S104) is signed off and stays untouched. Its S101 draws the Library but has no per-row Anvil / Workbench toggles, which the PRD now requires (requirements.md F7, last AC, and the resolution at ~l.519). Per the repo rule, a gap found before coding is raised as a mockup, not patched in code. This addendum is built from S101 as signed off: the settings tab strip Library · Scope · Behaviour, configure on collections, preview on cards, + Browse repo… + Import from vault… under each list, built-in = disable only, from repo / imported = disable and remove. Everything below is additive to S101.

Decisions already taken by the user (2026-11-11) — drawn as given, tagged D1–D4:
D1 — an imported or from-repo .base Collection shows in the Anvil Codex by embedding the .base through Bases, drawn with the Card chosen for that collection (our registered Card Bases view), with the same pill row and Card dropdown as S93. (L6)
D2 — today's Dataview / DataviewJS Views become Collections, listed as imported, migrated with Workbench on, Anvil off, so today's Workbench tabs stay (S96). The word "view" leaves the UI. (L1, L2, L3c, L7)
D3 — for the four built-in collections, the Workbench toggle controls whether that collection's section shows in the Workbench Codex tab (S95, follows the note). (L7)
D4 — Card preview (named in S101) is built in Phase 7 and gets its own state. (L5)
How to read this file. Light theme is the default; the Dark / Light toggle (top right) switches every figure, and L2b is always dark. The figures reuse S91–S104's CSS verbatim (.view, .set, .set-row, .cx-cats, .hero, .wb-sec…); new pieces use the lb- prefix. Tags: D# = user decision of 2026-11-11; PRD/SDD = fixed by the spec; P# = not specified, proposed here — accept the recommended default or change it. Nothing tagged P# is decided until you sign it off. Seed data is S91's (Wardens of Moonharbor), plus the S93 organizations and the S96 skills.

Proposals — your answer needed (recommended default in each)

  1. P1 — The enable checkbox and the two surface toggles (L2, L9). Options: (a) keep all three — the checkbox is the master switch, the toggles say where; (b) drop the checkbox and treat "both toggles off" as disabled. Recommended: (a). The checkbox is what the PRD's "disable" ACs and the DataviewJS consent gate attach to (enabled in the record). While it is off, the toggles keep their values but are inert (dimmed, aria-disabled), so re-enabling restores where it showed. Toggling both off does not uncheck; the row then says "Shown nowhere" (L9a). (b) would make re-enabling forget the surfaces and would make the consent prompt fire from a surface toggle.
  2. P2 — Surface defaults for a new collection (import or from repo). Recommended: by engine. Bases (.base import, every from-repo collection) → Anvil on, Workbench off — a .base is a grid over many notes, which is the Anvil's job. Dataview / DataviewJS → Workbench on, Anvil off, the same as the migration (D2), since these queries are usually written against the current note. Defaults apply without asking; the new row shows them and either toggle is one click away.
  3. P3 — Where Card preview opens and what it samples (L5). Recommended: inline, under the Card's row (like configure), one preview open at a time, no modal. Sample = the first entry of the first enabled collection that uses this Card; if none uses it, the first entry of the first enabled collection. A Sample from dropdown switches collection, so a mismatch (S104) can be checked before choosing the Card. The preview is read-only and inert: no navigation, no editor. It closes with Close preview, by pressing preview again, or Esc while focus is inside; focus returns to the preview button. With nothing to sample it says so (L5b) and draws no fake entry.
  4. P4 — How the toggles are labelled. Options: text-labelled switches; pressed-state chips; icons (⚒ / 🛠) with tooltips. Recommended: text-labelled switches, "Anvil" and "Workbench". The two words are the surface names the user already sees on the views; icons need a tooltip, which does not exist on mobile. Each switch is role="switch" with aria-label "Show Characters in the Anvil" / "… in the Workbench".
  5. P5 — What the Anvil selects after the shown collection is removed (L8). Recommended: no new rule — the existing CodexSelectionStore.resolve rule (PRD F3: "the first enabled collection is selected"), i.e. the first collection shown in the Anvil (Characters). Its remembered Card entry (cardByCollection) is deleted with it. A Workbench showing the removed collection's tab falls back to the Codex tab. The same applies when the collection is disabled or its Anvil toggle is turned off.
  6. P6 — What a built-in collection's "section" in the Workbench Codex tab contains (L7). S95 draws one Relations section; D3 needs one section per collection. Recommended: each section lists the entries of that collection linked from the followed note, with the relation name on the right, in Library order. This replaces S95's single Relations section (a recorded deviation from S95, not a silent one). Appears in stays as it is, because scenes are not a Library collection. A section with no linked entries is omitted.
  7. P7 — An imported collection in the Workbench. Recommended: an imported or from-repo collection with Workbench on becomes its own Workbench tab (S96's "a Workbench tab is a Collection shown in the Workbench"); only the four built-ins become sections in the Codex tab (D3). Tab order = Library order, after Codex and Navigator.
  8. P8 — A Dataview collection with the Anvil toggle on (L6b). D1 covers .base only. Recommended: allowed. The Codex body shows Dataview's own output in place of the card grid, and the Card dropdown is replaced by the text "Drawn by Dataview" (Cards draw Bases rows; a Dataview result is not one). Known limit, stated in the docs, not detected: a query that reads the current note shows little in the Anvil, which is why P2 defaults it off.
  9. P9 — Which part of a user's .base the Anvil uses (L6). A user's file may hold several views of its own. Recommended: the file's global filters, formulas and properties, plus the first view's filters and sort; that view's type is replaced by our Card view. Its other views are ignored, never written. The file is read, never patched (ADR-34).
  10. P10 — configure for a built-in (L3a). Recommended: a Tag field and Excluded folders with a "Same as Scope" checkbox (on by default; off reveals a per-collection list), and a live line "3 notes match". The label is not editable for a built-in. The S98 empty state's Change tag opens Library with this panel expanded and focus in the tag field.
  11. P11 — Row badges. Recommended: provenance as S101 (built-in, from repo, imported), replacing today's "Official"/"Imported" chips. An engine badge only on non-built-ins, using product names Bases, Dataview, DataviewJS (today: "bases", "dql", "dataviewjs"). A status pill only when something blocks the entry — "Consent required", "Dataview not installed", "Not available on mobile". Today's "Active" and "Disabled" pills go, because the checkbox already says that.
  12. P12 — Today's ⋯ row menu. Recommended: retired. Its items move into configure (L3c): View source → Open file; Edit (rename & command) → Name and Command fields; Re-review consent → Review consent…; Remove → the row's remove. One place per action.
  13. P13 — Telling the user their views moved (L2). Recommended: one dismissible line at the top of Collections, shown only when the migration moved at least one entry, dismissed for good via dismissedHints. No notice, no modal.
  14. P14 — Where the two settings with no obvious tab go (L1). Recommended: Curated bases folder moves to the Library, under the lists, renamed "Folder for collections from the repo" (it only says where Browse repo… installs files). The capability disclosure (T7.4, PRD F8: "stays reachable from settings") gets a link "What optional plugins add…" at the foot of the Library; its screen is T7.4's own mockup, not drawn here.
  15. P15 — S93's + Collection pill, now that toggles exist. Recommended: it opens a menu of enabled collections whose Anvil toggle is off; picking one turns that toggle on and selects the pill. The last item is "Manage in settings…". This is a deliberate menu choice, and it changes plugin settings, never a note.
  16. P16 — The inline remove confirmation (L8). Recommended: pressing remove opens a confirmation panel under the row (no modal, no confirm()). Focus lands on Cancel; Esc cancels. The text names what leaves which surface and says the vault file stays. After removal a notice repeats that, and focus moves to the next row's checkbox (or to + Browse repo… if it was the last row). Removing a Card in use names the collections that fall back to Hero (the registry already degrades to it).
  17. P17 — Narrow width (L2c). Recommended: below about 520px each row wraps onto two lines. Line 1: checkbox, name, badges. Line 2, indented under the name: the two switches, then configure and remove. Nothing is hidden behind a menu.
  18. P18 — The import refusal and the catalog browser are not redrawn here. PRD F7 ACs 7 and 9 (refused with a reason; a curated Dataview view installs) run through Import from vault… and Browse repo…. Recommended: keep today's import modal and its refusal text, with "view" replaced by "collection". If the catalog browser needs more than a list of rows with an Install button, draw it as a follow-up state (L10) before T7.2 codes it.
  19. P19 — Hero, the fallback Card (L4). Disabling or removing a Card sends its collections to Hero, so Hero itself must always exist. Recommended: Hero's checkbox is shown checked and inert, with the accessible description "Hero is the fallback Card and is always available". Table and Compact can be disabled like any built-in. This narrows PRD F7 AC 2 ("a built-in can be disabled") for one entry, so it needs your yes.

What this addendum commits us to

If you sign this off (with your answers to P1–P19), the following stop being open: (1) every Library collection row carries Anvil and Workbench switches beside its enable checkbox; Cards carry none; (2) settings split into Library · Scope · Behaviour exactly as L1c lists, with no setting dropped; (3) the Views list is gone: its entries are imported collections, migrated Workbench-on / Anvil-off, and its ⋯ menu's actions live in configure; (4) an imported or from-repo .base appears in the Anvil as a pill, embedded through Bases and drawn with the chosen Card; (5) a built-in's Workbench switch adds or removes its section in the Workbench Codex tab; an imported collection's adds or removes its tab; (6) configure is an inline panel: tag and excluded folders for built-ins, file and name for imports, name, source, command and consent for Dataview entries; (7) Card preview is inline, read-only and samples a real note, never a fake one; (8) remove confirms inline, says the vault file stays, and leaves no dangling selection, Card choice, pane or tab; (9) no step in the Library uses a confirm()/prompt() dialog. The only modal is today's DataviewJS consent modal, unchanged.
